grounding:
TITLE: The MiniMax-M2 Series: Mini Activations Unleashing Max Real-World Intelligence  
VENUE: arXiv:2605.26494v1 [cs.AI] 26 May 2026  
ONE-LINE TAKEAWAY: MiniMax-M2.7 achieves frontier-tier performance on agentic coding, reasoning, and office-task benchmarks with only 9.8B activated parameters per token, competing with larger closed-weight models.  
- Agentic workflows require long-horizon tasks that create efficiency and cost bottlenecks during training and inference.  
- Deployment in real-world settings demands solving complex, high-stakes tasks like production software engineering and knowledge-intensive automation.  
- Agent-driven data pipelines for agentic coding, cowork, reasoning, and knowledge tasks using executable workspaces and artifact-aligned rewards.  
- Forge, an agent-native RL system supporting white-box and black-box agents with windowed-FIFO scheduling, prefix-tree merging, and inference optimization.  
- Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture with 229.9B total parameters and 9.8B activated per token using sigmoid gating and fine-grained experts.  
- Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) module expanded to K=3 for speculative decoding during inference.  
- Self-evolution in M2.7: autonomous triage of failed training runs and modification of its own agent scaffold.  
- M2.7 scores 56.2 on SWE-bench Pro, 76.5 on SWE-bench Multilingual, 52.7 on Multi-SWE-bench, and 57.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.0.  
- On agentic cowork, M2.7 reaches 62.7 on MM Claw, 77.8 on BrowseComp, 50.0 on GDPval-AA, and 46.3 on Toolathlon.  
- On reasoning & knowledge, M2.7 posts 94.2 on AIME 2026 and 89.8 on GPQA-Diamond.  
- M2.7 is competitive with GPT-5.4 (57.7), Opus 4.6 (75.4), and Sonnet 4.6 (64.2) despite having only ~10B activated parameters.  
- M2.7 autonomously modifies its own agent scaffold and performs self-improvement on ML-engineering tasks.  
- 229.9B: total parameters in the M2 model.  
- 9.8B: number of activated parameters per token in M2.  
- 56.2: SWE-bench Pro score of M2.7.  
- 57.7: SWE-bench Pro score of GPT-5.4 (benchmark comparison).  
- Figure 1 shows performance of MiniMax-M2.7 versus closed-weight frontier baselines across agentic coding, agentic cowork, and reasoning & knowledge benchmarks.
